subtype: Friend who is struggling after failure [Observer]
passage:
Monday. Imran's result came out, and Imran had missed the cut-off by a few marks. Jahnavi noticed Imran skip lunch and mute the group chat.

Wednesday. Jahnavi did not send advice. Jahnavi knocked on the door with two cups of tea. "I'm just here. No pep talk." Imran spoke for ten minutes, mostly about feeling behind everyone.

Saturday. Jahnavi offered one practical thing: "I'm going to the library. I can hold you a seat." Imran came and sat with a book, opening nothing. Later Jahnavi added quietly that if the heaviness did not lift over the coming weeks, talking with the college counsellor might help. Imran said, "Maybe."

qa.q: What did Jahnavi bring on Wednesday?
qa.a: Jahnavi brought two cups of tea.

qa.q: What might Jahnavi have been worried about while watching Imran skip lunch and mute the chat?
qa.a: That Imran was withdrawing and in pain, and unsure how to help without pushing.

qa.q: What did Jahnavi do that helped more than advice would have?
qa.a: Offered company, listened, and offered small practical help such as holding a seat in the library.

qa.q: How might Imran have experienced Jahnavi's "No pep talk"?
qa.a: As a relief, allowing Imran to speak about feeling behind without being told to cheer up.

grounding: Shows a friend noticing withdrawal after a failure and offering company, listening and small help, with a gentle nudge toward a counsellor.

subtype: Friend who is struggling after failure [Observer]
passage: Asif, come here. I'm Aadhya, your Bua, and you're worried about your classmate who failed the entrance test, so let me tell you what I learned. When I was twenty-three my friend Sunil failed his exam for the second time. He stopped answering calls. I wrote him three long messages full of advice and got no reply. Then my mother said, "Go and sit with him." I went and said nothing clever. I brought vada pav, and we watched the street from his steps. After an hour he said, "I feel useless." I only nodded. Over the next weeks I carried his notebooks to the library and sat beside him. When he still could not sleep months later, I asked if he would try the college counsellor, and he did.

qa.q: What did Aadhya bring when going to sit with Sunil?
What might Aadhya have been feeling when the three long messages got no reply?
qa.a: Worried and helpless, unsure how to reach Sunil.

qa.q: What turning point changed how Aadhya helped?
qa.a: Aadhya's mother said to go and sit with him, so Aadhya went and offered company instead of advice.

qa.q: What might it have been like for Sunil when a friend simply sat beside him?
qa.a: Relieving, since it was after sitting with Aadhya for an hour that Sunil said "I feel useless".

grounding: Shows an elder recalling a friend who withdrew after failing, helped by company, small practical help and a nudge toward a counsellor.
